keyRules: In the Open category, the maximum height is 120 m, measured as the distance to the closest point of the ground surface — not simply straight down, so near a slope the ground beside you may also count. Within 50 m of a tall artificial obstacle (over 105 m), the entity responsible for it may request permission to fly up to 15 m above the obstacle's height.
Register as a UAS operator at tmcad.idronect.com (€25/year; visitors with an EASA operator number: €10 for 3 months)
The operator registration number or its QR code must be printed and affixed to the drone — the police may check, and failure to do so results in a penalty.
A1/A3 certificate required for drones over 250 g (online training, exam at the TM-CAD offices in Lija) — minimum age 16
Drones with class mark C1, C2 or C3 equipped with Remote ID must fly with Remote ID active and up to date, with the operator registration number entered in it.
Third-party insurance mandatory for drones of any weight
The ENTIRE country is controlled airspace — always check IDRONECT

In the Open category, you must keep the drone in your direct line of sight, with your own eyes only (glasses/contact lenses are fine; binoculars or a screen do not count) — or fly with the help of an observer, maintaining clear and effective communication between you at all times, so that together you can scan the airspace and avoid collisions. «Follow-me» mode is a separate exception, permitted up to 50 m from the pilot.
Do not fly over assemblies of people. Rules for uninvolved persons depend on subcategory, class mark and operating conditions; check the official matrix.

All of Malta is controlled airspace — every drone flight requires TM-CAD authorisation via tmcad.idronect.com. Many low-risk requests are approved automatically within a few minutes when the system confirms the flight is compliant; follow the conditions in your Authorisation Form. A separate 5 km no-fly zone covers the Malta International Airport area.

Flights that are not authorised automatically must be submitted at least 5 working days in advance. To fly in a restricted zone, upload a letter of permission ('no objection') from the zone owner in IDRONECT.
Night flying prohibited without specific authorisation

Valletta is a 'Special Permit Zone': commercial flights require a special permit, including a 'no objection' from the Office of the Prime Minister. For any other flight in Valletta and the other restricted zones, check the IDRONECT map and the authorisation conditions before flying.
importantNotes: The ENTIRE country is controlled airspace — every flight requires TM-CAD authorisation
Insurance mandatory for drones of any weight
Check the airport zones and other restricted zones on the IDRONECT map (tmcad.idronect.com/map)
Three-month registration (€10) for visitors who already have an EASA operator registration number; otherwise €25
GDPR applies when capturing images of identifiable people
Carry proof of registration, insurance, licence and authorisation — failure to do so can lead to fines. A flight without authorisation or outside its conditions can lead to confiscation of the drone.
